newsitem.title: INDIA: India Ranbaxy 96/97 net up 11 pct, sales to grow.
newsitem.headline: India Ranbaxy 96/97 net up 11 pct, sales to grow.

text.p: Indian pharmaceuticals firm Ranbaxy Laboratories Ltd on Friday announced an 11 percent increase in 196/97 (April-March) net profit, a dramatic drop from a 20.6 percent jump in first-half earnings.
The sharp slowdown was due to a decrease in income from the firm's activities in money markets, which the company had ploughed into its core pharmaceuticals business, chairman Parvinder Singh said.

"But our operating income has continued to rise, and our operating margins are significantly higher than the 22 percent increase in sales," Singh told a news conference to announce Ranbaxy's annual results without elaborating.
Ranbaxy said its net profit grew to 1.50 billion rupees in 1996/97 compared with 1.35 billion rupees in the previous year.
It said earnings per share on an increased equity base of 494 million rupees was 30.27 rupees against 30.42 rupees in the last year. Equity share capital in 1995/96 was 444 million rupees.
The firm's shares closed 3.25 rupees down at 644 rupees on the Bombay Stock Exchange.
Analysts said the results were positive.

"We expected a net profit of 1.54 billion rupees, helped by a sharp rise in the company's other income. But, it (other income) is lower, thus improving the quality of earnings," said Alroy Lobo, pharmaceuticals analyst at Kotak Securities.
Company president Davinder Singh Brar said he expected sales to grow by at least 20 percent in 1997/98 after reaching 10.66 billion rupees in 1996/97 from 8.77 billion the previous year.
The firm's chairman said earnings growth had been throttled by government controls on drug pricing, which cover 76 drugs and half of Ranbaxy's sales.
"Our earning ability is restricted by the government," Singh said. "The government's focus in on prices, while we maintain the first criteria must be availability and quality."
Brar said the firm, which earns more than half its revenue from exports, was focusing on selling dosage formulations rather than bulk drugs, where sales margins were low.

"Bulk drug sales in the domestic market after this year will be very, very negligible. Eventually, we would like all our business to be in dosages formulations, but we don't see that situation within the next five years," Brar said.
In 1996/97, the firm consolidated its presence in Russia, China, South Africa, Britain and the United States, Singh said.

Ranbaxy, which sells its products in 45 countries, controls a five percent share of the Indian pharmaceuticals market -- the largest after a seven percent share held by a subsidiary of Glaxo Wellcome Plc.
